288211.name: Grey Lady
288211.description: The Grey Lady was named for the people of Nantucket who have welcomed OCEARCH. The Grey Lady is the nickname of the Island that is hosting OCEARCH’s 27th expedition. It is also named for our friends at Cisco Brewery who have become partners and help enabled our work on the water. [A special thank you to Tammy Blades for sponsoring the SPOT tag.]

288212.name: Al
288212.description: Al is named after Al Perkinson, a visionary leader in conservation who served as the VP of Marketing for Costa Sunglasses. "To a man who has given so much to our journey! You have been a friend, a counselor, and true ocean champion through the highs and the lows. I know you would not have let us do this for you if we had asked… so from all of us at OCEARCH, this is our gift to you. If you can surprise me with a Fisch frame, I can surprise you with an Al - Tiger Shark in the Carolinas!" said Chris Fischer, Expedition Leader.

288213.name: J.D.
288213.description: J.D. was named by Jimmy Buffett during his visit to the M/V OCEARCH while on Expedition New York. It was an incredible moment having him on the ship while we had the opportunity to tag a small young of the year white shark pup. We look forward to tracking J.D. as he matures!

288214.name: Saltarina
288214.description: Named by Cesar from Galapagos National Park after the shark behavior, a quick jumper.

288215.name: Bezerra
288215.description: Ricardo Garla named Bezerra, in honor of the high school in Recife, Brazil Joao Berezza. The shark was captured by Brandon Eyre and Ricardo Garla (Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Norte).

288217.name: Chancellor Shark
288217.description: Chancellor Shark is a Shortfin Mako shark tagged during a research expedition by scientists with the Harte Research Institute’s Center for Sportfish Science and Conservation at Texas A&M University – Corpus Christi. “Chancellor John Shark” is named after the Chancellor of the Texas A&M University System, John Sharp. The Texas A&M University System is one of the largest higher education systems in the nation and comprised of 11 universities and 7 state agencies.

288218.name: Maya Marina
288218.description: Maya Marina was caught by Chad Banks during a research expedition and tagged by scientists at the Harte Research Institute’s Center for Sportfish Science and Conservation at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi. “Maya Marina” is named after Maya and Marina Corwin, who are the daughters of Jeff Corwin, and budding young biologists interested in sharks.

288219.name: Beamer
288219.description: Beamer was caught on the Blue Fin IV with Capt. Michael Potts by angler Mike D’Ecclesiis on July 28, 2013 during the Shark’s Eye Satellite Tag Tournament. The Montauk Public School 6th grade class named the blue shark Beamer.

288220.name: Emma
288220.description: Emma was named after Emma Darwin, the wife of Charles Darwin the English naturalist, scientist and author of “On the Origin of Species”.

288221.name: Princess Fi
288221.description: Ryan Johnson named Princess Fi after his wife.

288223.name: Pablo
288223.description: Cat Products named Pablo, with the help of OCEARCH fan Henry Holt, after Pablo Neruda, the Chilean poet-diplomat and politician who won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1971.

288224.name: DeMott
288224.description: Inspired by his sponsor, David DeMott was one of the four founders of SeaWorld in 1964. The data we gather on DeMott will continue to help us better understand how to protect him and his habitat. It’s all part of SeaWorld’s mission to inspire people to care for marine animals and the oceans they call home.

288227.name: Luis Antonio
288227.description: Luis named Luis Antonio after his son.

288228.name: Septima
288228.description: “Septima” is named in honor of American educator, civil rights activist and South Carolina native Septima Poinsette Clark. Septima was considered the “Queen Mother” of the civil rights movement, and established “Citizenship Schools” teaching reading to adults throughout the southern United States.

288229.name: Lyla Grace
288229.description: Chris Fischer named Lyla Grace after his daughter.

288231.name: Madaket Millie
288231.description: This shark was named after the Nantucket local legend Madaket Millie. She was a volunteer in 8 different decades for the US Coast Guard. She lived on Nantucket Island her entire life (1907 – 1990). This shark is named in honor of her patriotic life and unfaltering friendship to everyone on the Island. [A special thank you to Kathryn Florio for sponsoring the SPOT tag.]

288232.name: TJ
288232.description: TJ, rescued on a beach near Tijuana in May 2013, was near death when he arrived at SeaWorld’s Animal Health and Rescue Center. Severely dehydrated, malnourished and unable to swim on his own, our animal care and veterinary staff were concerned about his chances for survival. After nearly five months of medical care and rehabilitation at SeaWorld, TJ, who now weighed more than 75 pounds (gaining more than 20 pounds since his rescue), was ready to return to the ocean.

288233.name: Triton
288233.description: Triton was tagged by researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution about the MV Machaca. He was named by Emily Lockhart, a friend, and supporter of WHOI, in honor of the mythological fish-tailed sea god, Triton, who is a son of Poseidon and messenger of the sea. For more information visit www.camrinbraun.com.

288234.name: Merlin
288234.description: Merlin was tagged by researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI) aboard the MV Machaca. He was named by students at the Birches School (Lincoln, MA) and represents a legendary figure best known as a triumphant wizard who saved others from peril. The students hope Merlin the shark will serve as a symbol of our mission to save the ocean kingdom, much like the shark’s namesake. For more information on the science being conducted with this tagging effort, visit www.camrinbraun.com

288235.name: Machaca
288235.description: Machaca was tagged by researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution and was named for the vessel he was tagged on, the MV Machaca, owned and operated by Captain Willy Hatch in Falmouth, MA. For more information visit www.camrinbraun.com.

288236.name: Lady Kemma
288236.description: After rainy days and a Tsunami warning, we finally found Lady Kemma. Our last female to be tagged in Playa Hermosa. Her name is also inspired by a Houstonian teacher part of our outreach program #TAMUSeaTurtleTrackingProject, whose dear friend was flooded out during hurricane Harvey, but who is fighting back to recover and get back to teaching. If you are interested to read about what else we are doing, you can follow our field work on http://plotkinlabtamu.wix.com/plotkinlab#!blog/b7vfl.

288237.name: Hudson
288237.description: Hudson is named after the river. The river is named after Henry Hudson, an Englishman sailing for the Dutch East India Company, who explored it in 1609, and after whom Canada’s Hudson Bay is also named.

288238.name: Orlando
288238.description: This female tiger shark was named in honor of the Orlando community.

288239.name: Joseph
288239.description: Joseph is a 10 ft tiger shark named by fans of Cat Products after a town in Texas. Joseph is the second shark tagged during Expedition Gulf of Mexico.

288243.name: Elias
288243.description: Dave Grime caught this hammerhead in the Carl Darenberg Memorial Shark’s Eye Tournament in Montauk, angler Dave Grimes gave the volunteer observer the opportunity to name the hammerhead. She chose Elias. Dr. Greg Skomal said, “the tagging of the smooth hammerhead is a milestone.”

288244.name: Bonac
288244.description: Bonac was tagged during the 2nd Annual Shark’s Eye Tournament and Festival, which is an all catch and release shark tournament held in Montauk, NY. This shark was captured by Joe Gaviola and the crew of the Free Nicky and named by the school children at the Amagansett School. The name Bonac honors the original settlers of Springs, in the northern part of East Hampton Town — the Bonackers.

288245.name: Genie
288245.description: To honor the founder of Mote Marine Laboratory, Dr. Greg Skomal chose to name Genie after Eugenie Clark. Eugenie who became known as "the shark lady" started studying sharks back in the '50s and still does to this very day. "She's a very special lady who inspired us all," says Skomal.

288246.name: George
288246.description: George was named for Expedition Leader Chris Fischer’s father. Chris named Mary Lee after his mother and has been waiting for a male shark to name after his father who has supported Chris and his vision for OCEARCH. Now George and Mary Lee are together in the Atlantic Ocean creating a greater public awareness for sharks and the ocean. [A special thank you to Bob Holding for sponsoring the SPOT tag.]

288248.name: Ciona
288248.description: Ciona was tagged by researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution aboard the MV Machaca. He was named to honor Anna Ciona, a seven year old shark enthusiast from Calgary, Canada. For more information visit www.camrinbraun.com.

288249.name: Manhattan
288249.description: This young white shark is named after Manhattan. We hope the tracking of these sharks near by the city will help connect people to our ocean movement.

288250.name: Bailey
288250.description: "Bailey" is named in honor of Bailey Symington, a longtime supporter of the Lowcountry Institute on Spring Island, SC, and many other conservation organizations. She is a great supporter of the arts, an avid naturalist and a beloved member of the low country community.

288251.name: Harry Etta
288251.description: The Hampton Wildlife Fund, Inc. is a charitable organization whose mission is to assist in educational and other endeavors that contribute to the conservation and protection of the wildlife and marine resources of the State of SC. The Fund, established in 1981, is named for Harry R.E. Hampton, South Carolina's first true conservationist. Thus, "Harry-Etta" is appropriately named in his memory. Please visit www.hamptionwildlifefund.org on the web or on Facebook.

288252.name: Sandy Lu
288252.description: Sandy Lu is the last turtle we equipped with a satellite tag in Rio Oro. She was the only one that night that had no eggs or follicles left and she is likely to embark on her post-nesting migration after leaving the beach. If you are interested to read about what else we are doing, you can follow our field work on http://plotkinlabtamu.wix.com/plotkinlab#!blog/b7vfl.

288254.name: Maya
288254.description: Enrico named Maya after his daughter.

288255.name: ANZAC
288255.description: This tiger shark, tagged on Ningaloo Reef, was named in honor of the veterans in Australia and New Zealand. ANZAC national days is celebrated on April 25th.

288256.name: Maia
288256.description: Maia is the third turtle to be tracked from Kyparissia Bay in 2018. In Greek mythology, Maia is the daughter of Atlas and the mother of Hermes (the god of communication and connectivity).

288257.name: Susan
288257.description: Susan is named for Susan G. Komen; Peoria native and breast cancer survivor.

288258.name: Hal
288258.description: Hal is a 12’ 6” white shark named by our partner SeaWorld for the people of Halifax, Nova Scotia.

288259.name: Viper
288259.description: Viper is named in honor of the Space Coast Junior / Senior High School in Cocoa, Florida. The school drove two hours to visit the ship in Jacksonville, Florida! We are inspired by the teachers and students passion for the ocean.

288260.name: CubsWin
288260.description: Cubswin was tagged by researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution aboard the MV Machaca. He was named by Daphne Hoch Cunningham to commemorate the Chicago Cubs’ 2016 World Series title. Daphne is a Corporation member of the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution. For more information visit www.camrinbraun.com.

288261.name: Leon III
288261.description: Dr. Julio Lamilla named this shark after León Tercero Matamala, a permanent assistant in the Laboratory of Ichthiology of the Universidad Austral in Valdivia, Chile. He devoted his life to science, always ready to help both in field and lab. He died of a brain tumor in February of 2013.

288262.name: AB
288262.description: A.B. was named after OCEARCH Chief Engineer Mark Bowden’s brother Adam. Mark brought the ship back from Australia to the United States and has been with us since early 2015. We are honored to have him as part of our team.

288263.name: Beatriz
288263.description: Cat Products named Beatriz after Beatriz Parra Durango, Ecuador’s foremost classical soprano.

288264.name: Miss Lillie
288264.description: Miss Lillie was tagged by scientists of The Nature Conservancy using a SPOT tag during a shark fisheries-independent monitoring cruise off Sarasota Bay in Florida in collaboration with Mote Marine Laboratory. “Miss Lillie” is named after Lillie Langtry, a celebrated European actress who became the inspiration of Judge Roy Bean, "The Law West of the Pecos [River]" along the Rio Grande, and named Langtry, Texas after her (although they never met in life she visited Langtry after the Judge passed).

288265.name: Carl
288265.description: Caught by the crew of the Free Nicky in the Carl Darenberg Memorial Shark’s Eye Tournament, the mako was named after tournament founder, the late Carl Darenberg. “It was a great honor for me to name that fish after my lifelong friend,” said the tournament winner Joe Gaviola. “I fished in one of Carl’s first tournaments in 1973 with my dad. It is very exciting to see how his shark tournament has evolved."

288266.name: Oprah
288266.description: Oprah was named by expedition leader Chris Fischer. Fischer named her after Oprah Winfrey, one of America's great philanthropists who has done much with education in Africa.

288267.name: Maroochy
288267.description: Update May 2016: Australian Tiger shark Maroochy was caught and killed on a drum line in Bunderburg, which is part of the Queensland Shark Control Program. Maroochy was tagged on the OCEARCH near Fraser Island in February 2015 and spent her time between Bunderburg and Fraser. She was in the area with the baited drum lines several times before she was caught and killed.

288268.name: Crystal (Tiger)
288268.description: This female tiger shark is named after Crystal Pier at Wrightsville Beach, NC.

288270.name: Savannah
288270.description: Savannah was named to celebrate the people of Savannah, GA. The OCEARCH team was humbled by their hospitality and passion for the ocean. Savannah was tagged during Lowcountry Expedition.

288271.name: Lal
288271.description: Lal is the fifth green sea turtle tagged of the 2019 season. Researchers from the Conservancy of Southwest Florida tagged Lal after she was encountered on Keewaydin Island, Florida. She had been previously seen nesting on the same beach in past seasons. Lal will be part of a study to learn more about the post-nesting movements and migratory pathways of green sea turtles that nest on the gulf coast of Florida. All research authorized by Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission.

288272.name: Cate Ells
288272.description: Cate Ells was tagged during the 2nd Annual Shark’s Eye Tournament and Festival, which is an all catch and release shark tournament held in Montauk, NY. This shark was captured by Wendy Benchley, wife of the late Peter Benchley, author of Jaws, on board the Reel Intensity and was named after Wendy’s two granddaughters Catharine and Eloise.

288274.name: Venus
288274.description: Venus is female we found her as she was heading head back to the water. The beach she came up on to nest is close to the border with Nicaragua and in the middle of an abundant fishing ground. If you are interested to read about what else we are doing, you can follow our field work on http://plotkinlabtamu.wix.com/plotkinlab#!blog/b7vfl.

288277.name: Trinity
288277.description: Cat Dealer Hastings Deering brought the OCEARCH team to speak at the Trinity Bay State High School during the first expedition in Australia. Trinity the tiger shark is named after the school and for all students who will track her movements.

288278.name: Beaufort
288278.description: Beaufort is a immature male Tiger Shark that was tagged during the Lowcountry Expedition. We look forward to sharing our data so that the people of Beaufort can continue to monitor the migration of this immature Tiger Shark.

288281.name: Alice
288281.description: Named after Alice Springs in the Northern Territory of Australia. Alice Springs is situated in the geographic center of Australia near the southern border of the Northern Territory.

288282.name: Harvey
288282.description: Harvey was tagged by scientists at the Harte Research Institute’s Center for Sportfish Science and Conservation at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi. “Harvey” is named after Harvey Weil, the grandson of Chuck Weil and the great-grandson of the renowned sportsman Harvey Weil. Harvey Weil, Sr., was dedicated to the preservation of nature and sportsmanship, which he instilled in his entire family, including his great-grandson.

288283.name: Isabela
288283.description: Named after Isabela Island in the Galapagos Islands.

288285.name: Azlyn
288285.description: Azlyn Grey was named by our great friend and colleague, Alisa Newton (Harley), Head of Aquatic Health at WCS' New York Aquarium. It has been a pleasure working with Harley over the past few expeditions. All the hard work and dedication she has poured into the future health of our world's oceans has made the decision to have her name this shark an easy one.

288286.name: Melanie
288286.description: Melanie is the fourth green sea turtle tagged of the 2019 season. Through a collaborative effort, researchers from the Conservancy of Southwest Florida and the Sanibel-Captiva Conservation Foundation tagged Melanie after she successfully laid a nest on Sanibel Island, Florida. Melanie will be part of a study to learn more about the post-nesting movements and migratory pathways of green sea turtles that nest on the gulf coast of Florida. All research authorized by Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission.

288287.name: Kathryn
288287.description: Alison Kock named Kathryn after her sister.

288288.name: Chessie
288288.description: The name Chessie comes from the Chechessee River in Port Royal Sound, South Carolina where the Port Royal Sound Maritime Center is located. The mission of the Maritime Center is to connect people with the waters and the lands of Port Royal Sound.

288290.name: Marcella
288290.description: Jody named Marcella after his girlfriend.

288291.name: Sofia
288291.description: Captain Brett McBride named Sofia after his daughter.

288292.name: Gratitude
288292.description: This shark is named in gratitude for what the ocean has given us.

288293.name: Harry Ette
288293.description: The Hampton Wildlife Fund Inc. is a charitable organization whose mission is to assist in educational and other endeavors that contribute to the conservation and protection of the wildlife and marine resources of the SC. The Fund, established in 1981, is named for Harry R.E. Hampton, South Carolina’s first true conservationist. Thus, “Harry-Ette” is appropriately named in his memory. Please visit www.hamptonwildlifefund.org on the web or on Facebook.

288294.name: Marilin
288294.description: Marilin is named after Marilin Cruz, the director of the Galapagos bio-security agency and sister of the Charles Darwin Foundation’s sub-director Felipe Cruz.

288295.name: Success
288295.description: Chris Fischer named Success because he believed their expedition in South Africa was a success.

288296.name: Elaia
288296.description: Last but not least we have Elaia; the final turtle to be tracked by ARCHELON in 2018. Elaia is a coastal village at the core nesting area of Kyparissia Bay. Elaia was also a goddess half-angel half-demon in Greek mythology, often accompanied by nymphs and elves (xotika).

288298.name: Aussie
288298.description: Named after the great country of Australia, home of OCEARCH’s 21st and 22nd expeditions. “Ausssi Aussie Aussie Oi Oi Oi!”

288299.name: Luis
288299.description: Cat Products named Luis, with the help of OCEARCH fan Kay Brimage-Minkel, after Luis Urzúa, the Chilean miner from the 2010 mining accident who mobilized a team who worked together to ensure that every man survived and thrived in the worst of conditions.

288300.name: Lydia
288300.description: Lydia was named after the founder of Bradley University, a long time friend of Caterpillar.

288302.name: Sherril
288302.description: Named for Sherrill West the first woman to achieve the position of Vice President at Caterpillar. She was instrumental in solidifying Caterpillar’s position as a technology leader.

288303.name: Mariela
288303.description: We found Mariela while she was heading up the beach to nest. She laid 81 eggs and she had no follicles or eggs left in her ovaries or oviducts after nesting. While we installed the satellite transmitter it started raining pretty heavily, but the epoxy dried just fine and after her release, she happily dashed back to the sea. f you are interested in what else we are doing, you can follow our field work on http://plotkinlabtamu.wix.com/plotkinlab#!blog/b7vfl.

288304.name: Jedda
288304.description: Jedda was named after the Australian movie Jedda, the first film to star two aboriginal actors in leading roles. Cat Products fan Schwarz Wolf submitted Jedda’s name. Jedda is the first shark tagged during the east Australia expedition.

288305.name: Lonesome Jorgita
288305.description: Yasmania from Galapagos National Park named Lomesome Jorgita. Lonesome George, a giant tortoise from the island of Pinta in the northern regions of the Galapagos Archipelago, was the last known survivor of the Pinta tortoise (Chelonoidis abingdoni). He was considered one of the rarest creatures in the world and became a conservation icon. Lonesome George was born before 1912 and died June 24, 2012.

288306.name: Leeuwin
288306.description: Leeuwin, the tiger shark, is named after the Leeuwin current. The Leeuwin current is a warm ocean current, which flows southwards near the western coast of Australia. It rounds Cape Leeuwin to enter the waters south of Australia where its influence extends as far as Tasmania.

288308.name: Hannah
288308.description: Dr. Adam Barnett of TropWATER at James Cook University in partnership with OCEARCH tagged Hannah on Batt Reef, Queensland, Australia

288309.name: Emily
288309.description: Emily is the second green sea turtle tagged of the 2019 season. Researchers from the Conservancy of Southwest Florida tagged Emily after she was encountered on Keewaydin Island, Florida. She had been previously seen in 2017 on the same beach. Emily will be part of a study to learn more about the post-nesting movements and migratory pathways of green sea turtles that nest on the gulf coast of Florida. All research authorized by Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission.

288310.name: Sabrina
288310.description: Sabrina was double-tagged by Mote Marine Laboratory scientists with a fin-mounted SPOT5 transmitter, for near real time location information, as well as a pop-up archival tag. Together these satellite tags will provide data that will contribute to our understanding of the movement, migration, and habitat utilization of Bull Sharks along the Florida Gulf coast.

288311.name: Jessica
288311.description: Jessica was a solitary nesting female at Ostional. She was biding her time while we went through the installation process for the transmitter and then lost no time in making her way back to the water. If you are interested in reading about what else we are doing, you can follow our field work on http://plotkinlabtamu.wix.com/plotkinlab#!blog/b7vfl.

288312.name: Corale
288312.description: We had been patrolling different nesting beaches for almost two weeks without seeing a single nesting turtle when we finally found Corale. It was a rainy night, but that didn’t matter to Corale and she laid 112 eggs. If you are interested to read about what else we are doing, you can follow our field work on http://plotkinlabtamu.wix.com/plotkinlab#!blog/b7vfl.

288313.name: Sellendilloh
288313.description: Darrel named Sellendilloh. Sellendilloh means long-time-longing.

288314.name: Polymnia
288314.description: Polymnia is the second turtle tagged in Kyparissia Bay this summer. In Greek mythology, Polymnia was one of the nine Muses. The name translates as many songs!

288316.name: Hunter
288316.description: Hunter was tagged by scientists at the Harte Research Institute’s Center for Sportfish Science and Conservation at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi. The shark was named after Hunter Stunz meaning the “one who hunts.” Hunter (the human) is a budding young eight-year-old future marine biologist fascinated by hammerhead sharks. Hunter (the shark) was tagged near an oil and gas platform off the Texas coast.

288317.name: Lazarus
288317.description: Lazarus was tagged by recreational anglers Dwade Hickey and Eric Ozolins working with the scientists at the Harte Research Institute’s Center for Sportfish Science and Conservation at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi. According to our reports, Lazarus is the largest Mako caught in the surf in the western Gulf of Mexico…not once, but twice! It is very rare to catch a Mako from shore, especially one of this size! (Photo credit: Eric Ozolins)

288318.name: Brunswick I
288318.description: Brunswick is a 4 ft 54 lb male young of the year white shark tagged on August 22, 2016, during Expedition New York. This shark was named after the Brunswick School in Greenwich, Connecticut.

288320.name: Thalia
288320.description: This is the penultimate turtle to receive a satellite tag at Kyparissia Bay in 2018. Thalia was one of the Nereides, the ancient goddesses of the sea...

288321.name: Lori Anne
288321.description: Lori Anne was tagged by Mote Marine Laboratory scientists with a fin-mounted SPOT5 transmitter that will provide near real-time location data for her for up to a year. This information will help us understand how she uses the habitat available to her in Boca Grande Pass and Charlotte Harbor as a whole, as well as track her annual migration.

288322.name: Andrea
288322.description: Andrea is the first green sea turtle tagged of the 2019 season. Researchers from the Sanibel-Captiva Conservation Foundation tagged Andrea after she successfully laid a nest on Sanibel Island, Florida. She had been previously encountered laying eggs two years earlier in 2017 on the same beach. Andrea will be part of a study to learn more about the post-nesting movements and migratory pathways of green sea turtles that nest on the gulf coast of Florida. All research authorized by Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission.

288323.name: CHIPS
288323.description: The OCEARCH team visited the Camp Hill Infants and Primary School while in Brisbane. The school then ran a competition and nominated the name C.H.I.P.S.

288324.name: Mission
288324.description: Mission was named after Mission Bay, San Diego, where SeaWorld first began its conservation research. The research performed has led to groundbreaking marine reproductive science, as well as a tremendous amount of conservation over the years.

288326.name: Errol Finn
288326.description: Errol Finn was tagged by researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI) aboard the MV Machaca. He was named by the Cunningham Hoch family, longtime ocean advocates and friends of WHOI. For more information on the science being conducted with this tagging effort, visit www.camrinbraun.com.

288327.name: Sunny
288327.description: Sunshine Beach State School is where Sarah and Lyla Fischer attended school while the OCEARCH was working in Australia. We were thrilled to name a shark Sunny so the kids from the school can follow Sunny the shark while they learn from the OCEARCH STEM curriculum.

288328.name: Ned
288328.description: Ned is named after Edward “Ned” Kelly the famous Australian bush ranger. He was named by Caterpillar fan Clapton Robertson

288331.name: Olivia
288331.description: We found Olivia nesting during a calm, dark night. She only laid 80 eggs, which might be due to her being done with nesting for the season. The ultrasound images showed us that she had no structures left in either her ovaries or oviducts, which means she should soon start her post-nesting migration. If you are interested to know what else we are up to, you can follow our field work on http://plotkinlabtamu.wix.com/plotkinlab#!blog/b7vfl.

288332.name: Miss Costa
288332.description: Miss Costa was named for our long time friends and partner Costa Sunglasses. Costa has done so much to enable our work on the water and we have been waiting to name a female white shark in honor of our partnership with them. We can’t wait to see where she will go!

288333.name: Katharine
288333.description: Katharine, who was tagged off Cape Cod, Massachusetts, was named by Cat Products fans in honor of Katharine Lee Bates, a Cape Cod native and songwriter - best known for her poem and song "America The Beautiful", which has been called "an expression of patriotism at its finest."

288334.name: Weimar
288334.description: Weimar was named after Ruth Weimar who generously hosted the OCEARCH team in Georgia. She connected us to Brunswick and Savannah, making Lowcountry the most inclusive expedition to date.

288335.name: Berlanga
288335.description: Named by Gonzallo from Galapagos National Park after Thomas de Berlanga who discovered Galapagos Island. Chris Fischer and Alex Hearn also had the privilege to speak to a local school named after Berlanga during Expedition Galapagos.

288336.name: Nickol
288336.description: Luke Leech from Nickol Bay Sport Fishing Club named this tiger shark after Nickol Bay where they have learned a great deal about tiger sharks and is an area commonly used by the local recreational anglers. The club is interested in the conservation and research of tiger sharks.

288337.name: Teddy
288337.description: "Teddy the shark was named after Theodore Roosevelt, one of the original founders of WCS and one of our collaborators on this expedition,” said Chris Fischer, Founding Chairman and Expedition Leader. "I also had the great privilege of planning this New York expedition on Teddy Roosevelt's table at the Explorers Club in Manhattan.

288338.name: Vindication
288338.description: During our 2012 expedition off South Africa, the team was temporarily shut down due to a fatal shark attack. After almost a month of being shut down, the crew was finally allowed to continue the expedition and Vindication was the first shark tagged.

288339.name: Lemanja
288339.description: Iemanjá is a beautiful, healthy female shark with striking colors and a gentle swim. She is named after an Orisha spirit from the African culture that is beloved in this region and is also regarded as the Queen of the Oceans.

288340.name: Sage
288340.description: “Sage" was named in remembrance of Perihan, a beloved teacher at Southampton High School and member of Shinnecock’s Perry Nation. The name “Sage” carries special significance to Perihan, and we are honored to aid in her tribute.

288343.name: Mackay
288343.description: Cat dealer Hastings Deering brought the OCEARCH team to speak at the Mackay State School during our first expedition in Australia. Mackay is named after the school and for all students to follow.

288344.name: Sero
288344.description: Sero was tagged by scientists at BioPixel Oceans Foundation.

288347.name: Caroline Mae
288347.description: Caroline Mae was tagged by scientists at the Harte Research Institute’s Center for Sportfish Science and Conservation at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi. “Caroline Mae” is named after Caroline Wetz of Corpus Christi, TX, a young girl with a love for the ocean. She is concerned about the growing marine debris problem in our oceans and how that can affect marine life. She wants all of us to be better stewards of our environment and help protect all ocean animals!

288348.name: Enric
288348.description: The tiger shark was named after National Geographic explorer in residence Enric Sala, head of the Pristine Seas Initiative, which aims to help protect the last wild places in the ocean. Charles Darwin Foundation tagged the shark in collaboration with OCEARCH.

288349.name: Pat
288349.description: Named for Pat Mullins for her love of children and grandchildren

288350.name: Tony
288350.description: After a heavy thunderstorm, we went patrolling and the first turtle we found was Tony. Tony is named in honor of Conservationist, Scientist, and Animal Hero Tony Amos, who passed away recently. Tony was the founder of the ARK, an animal rehabilitation center that was severely damaged by Hurricane Harvey.  If you are interested to read about what else we are doing, you can follow our field work on http://plotkinlabtamu.wix.com/plotkinlab#!blog/b7vfl.

288351.name: Jacob
288351.description: Jacob was tagged by recreational anglers Scott Nelson and Eric Ozolins in collaboration with scientists at the Harte Research Institute’s Center for Sportfish Science and Conservation at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi. The shark was named after Jacob Wetz, a budding 6-year-old future marine biologist who has been enthralled with sharks since he could first talk. One of his future goals is to become a SCUBA diver so he can see sharks in their natural environment.

288352.name: iSimangaliso
288352.description: Dr. Adam Barnett tagged this mature female tiger shark. iSimangaliso means miracle in the local language and it also the name of the world heritage wetland park in the area.

288354.name: Jefferson
288354.description: Jefferson is the second shark we tagged in Nova Scotia waters. It’s a privilege to name him after Jefferson's Bourbon, whose commitment to our mission over the years has funded our expeditions to tag sharks in countries around the world. Their support is directly contributing to an abundant future for our children. Jefferson is 12-feet 7.5-inches long and was tagged just off Hirtle’s Beach in beautiful Nova Scotia.

288355.name: Dr Brent
288355.description: Dr. Brent was rescued by Pacific Marine Mammal Center on April 22, 2018, at San Onofre State Beach north of San Diego, and was immediately taken to SeaWorld San Diego for treatment and rehabilitation. While thin and emaciated, she was responsive. She received antibiotics during her rehabilitation and was later fed a mixture of herring, capelin, mackerel, sardines, and squid daily.

288356.name: Betsy
288356.description: Caterpillar Inc. fans named Betsy after "Old Betsy," the nickname given to the prototype of Caterpillar's first diesel engine model.

288357.name: Judy
288357.description: Judy was named after one of the founders of Costa Sunglasses, a longtime friend and partner in conservation. “We support the OCEARCH mission to replace fear with facts when it comes to learning more about the ocean’s giants,” said Al Perkinson, vice president of marketing for Costa Sunglasses. “The more we can understand about how the oceans function, the better equipped we’ll be to help protect them.”

288359.name: Miss May
288359.description: Miss May was the first white shark tagged during OCEARCH's Expedition NASFA. The 10-foot white shark was named after Mayport, FL which will be OCEARCH's future headquarters!

288360.name: Riley
288360.description: Denny named Riley after his son.

288364.name: Canyon
288364.description: Canyon was tagged by researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution in partnership with local conservation advocates as part of the TOTEM project. He was tagged aboard the MV Endurance in the recently designated Northeast Canyons and Seamounts Marine National Monument, his namesake. For more information, visit the TOTEM project website: www.simonthorrold.com/totem/

288365.name: Catalina
288365.description: Named by Cat Parts Miami in support of Caterpillar’s sustainability efforts.

288371.name: Jaimie
288371.description: Jaimie was tagged during the 2nd Annual Shark’s Eye Tournament and Festival, which is an all catch and release shark tournament held in Montauk, NY. This shark was captured by Joe Gaviola and Nick Racanelli on the Free Nicky. Jaimie is named after Nick’s daughter.

288372.name: Borinquena
288372.description: Borinqueña was tagged by scientists working with Mote Marine Laboratory. Her name means female from Puerto Rico based on the Taino name for Puerto Rico.

288373.name: Finley
288373.description: Finley is a 10 ft female tiger shark in the Gulf of Mexico tagged during #ExpeditionGoMex. Finely was named in collaboration with Shark Week with your help!

288374.name: Charli
288374.description: Charli was rescued by Newport Animal Control at Newport Beach, CA on May 23, 2018. She was then taken in by the Pacific Marine Mammal Center (PMMC) for initial care. While in good body condition and active, Charli was entangled in fishing line around her neck. PMMC staff removed the entanglement and stabilized her condition by giving her oral electrolytes and subcutaneous fluids.

288375.name: Azul
288375.description: Azul was named by our good friend, Carl Safina. He is the author of various books and many other writings about how the ocean is changing, lives of free-living animals, and the human relationship with the natural world. #DontFearTheFin

288376.name: Shelly
288376.description: After we were about to give up hope to find another depleted turtle (without follicles or eggs in her ovaries or oviducts) on our last night in Hacienda Baru, we found Shelly. She laid 83 eggs and we hope that she will travel far on her post-nesting migration. If you are interested to read about what else we are doing, you can follow our field work on http://plotkinlabtamu.wix.com/plotkinlab#!blog/b7vfl.

288377.name: Hans
288377.description: Hans was tagged by Eric Ozolins in collaboration with scientists at the Harte Research Institute’s Center for Sportfish Science and Conservation at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi. Hans was named by Newman “Tree” Baker and family in memory of Hans the Sand Tiger Shark, a long-term resident of the Texas State Aquarium in Corpus Christi. Hans the Scalloped Hammerhead was tagged off the beach along Padre Island National Seashore.

288379.name: Itabaca
288379.description: Tiger shark Itabca was named after the canal where the crew found the four tigers on the last day of the expedition.

288380.name: Martie
288380.description: Martie was tagged by scientists with the Harte Research Institute’s Center for Sportfish Science and Conservation at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi during a research cruise on the Scat Cat of the Fisherman’s Wharf. “Martie” is named for after the surname Martin in honor of their Great Grandfather, Frank Gerig. Frank worked for the U.S. Corps of Engineers building the Panama Canal in the early 1900s. In the 1970s, the Corps launched a Hopper Dredge Vessel named GERIG to help keep U.S. waterways open. Martie the Shortfin Mako shark now swims those same channels.

288381.name: Hilton
288381.description: Hilton was caught off the coast of Hilton Head, SC during the Lowcountry Expedition. Hilton was named after the local community who has graciously welcomed us. Hilton was also tagged on the anniversary of Lydia.

288382.name: Adelaide
288382.description: Named after Adelaide, South Australia's capital.

288384.name: Jax
288384.description: “Jax” is named after two beautiful twins, Joanne and Maxine, born on October 10, 2014. As they grow up we hope they will have the opportunity to enjoy and appreciate the Port Royal Sound for its beauty and ecological significance. Jax was tagged by Bryan Frazier in partnership with OCEARCH.

288385.name: Isabella
288385.description: Isabella was tagged during the 2nd Annual Shark’s Eye Tournament and Festival, which is an all catch and release shark tournament held in Montauk, NY. This shark was captured by Joe Gaviola and the crew of the Free Nicky and named after the granddaughter of the donor of the tag Austin Marxe.

288386.name: Irma
288386.description: We had to fend off a whole family of raccoons that wanted to steal Irma's eggs (111 of them). Raccoons are some of the natural predators of sea turtle eggs and babies, but due to a decline in bigger predators like coyotes, the raccoon populations are now out of control and are endangering already endangered species like sea turtles. If you are interested to read about what else we are doing, you can follow our field work on http://plotkinlabtamu.wix.com/plotkinlab#!blog/b7vfl.

288388.name: Cathy
288388.description: Cathy is named after Australian gold medalist Cathy Freeman, the second Australian Aboriginal Olympic champion. In 2000 she won the gold in the 400 M race in Sydney.

288389.name: Cabot
288389.description: Cabot is a 9’ 8”, juvenile white shark. Our partner SeaWorld named him using suggestions from Nova Scotians after the explorer John Cabot.

288390.name: Thalassa
288390.description: To kick off World Turtle Day (June 16th) we tagged our fourth turtle of the summer in Kyparissia Bay. In Greek mythology, Thalassa was the primeval spirit of the Mediterranean Sea. Coupling with her male counterpart Pontus, she spawned the species of fish.

288391.name: Brenda
288391.description: After her travels in South Africa near places such as Dyer Island, Quoin Rock Island, Duiwenhoksriviermond Private Nature Reserve, Brenda traveled north along the coast up to Mozambique. Tragically in October of 2012, she was captured in a gill net and killed. Use this link to read the press release please: http://bit.ly/VlFfu8

288392.name: Quang
288392.description: Named after Quang cyclone that occurred during Expedition West Australia.

288393.name: Gabriela
288393.description: Cat Products named Gabrela, with the help of OCEARCH fan Christina Penner, after Gabriela Mistral, the pseudonym of Lucila Godoy Alcayaga, a Chilean poet-diplomat, educator and feminist who was the first Latin American to win the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1945.

288394.name: Don
288394.description: Don was tagged by researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution aboard the MV Machaca. He was named by Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution Trustee Jean Tempel. For more information visit www.camrinbraun.com.

288396.name: Yolanda
288396.description: Esperanza means hope in Spanish. As we close Expedition Galapagos we leave hopeful for a change and conservation of the Galapagos Marine Reserve as well as all the Easter Pacific. We hope that the local institutions will continue the arduous work on land and on the ocean.

288397.name: Peggy Hughes
288397.description: Peggy Hughes was caught by angler William Fay during a research expedition and tagged by scientists with the Harte Research Institute’s Center for Sportfish Science and Conservation at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi. “Peggy” is named after Peggy Hughes, an avid outdoorswoman and strong supporter of marine and wildlife conservation from San Antonio, Texas.

288399.name: Kimberley
288399.description: Our friends Caterpillar named this beautiful tiger shark Kimberley after one of the 9 regions of Western Australia. She was tagged Ningaloo Reef on the first day of Expedition West Australia.

288400.name: Milt
288400.description: Inspired by her sponsor, Milt Shedd was one of the four founders of SeaWorld in 1964. The data we gather on Milt will continue to help us better understand how to protect her and her habitat. It’s all part of SeaWorld’s mission to inspire people to care for marine animals and the oceans they call home.

288401.name: Perseverance
288401.description: Chris Fischer named Perseverance. The crew hadn't caught a shark for 5 days, and then they caught Perseverance.

288402.name: Caroline
288402.description: Caroline is the 4th of four white sharks sampled, tagged, and studied in Feb 2019 during the first NASFA Expedition from North Florida to S. Caroline. She was tagged 10 miles off of Hilton Head.

288404.name: Miguel
288404.description: Juan named Miguel after his brother.

288405.name: Madiba
288405.description: Chris Fischer named Madiba after Nelson Mandela. Madiba was caught and killed on a drumline at Sunwich Port on the KwaZulu-Natal South Coast in January, 2013.

288407.name: Jane
288407.description: Jane is the first female white shark ever SPOT tagged in Canadian waters. The 10-foot long shark was named her after Captain Brett’s mother.

288408.name: Thomas
288408.description: Thomas is a mature male blue shark caught and tagged by researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution aboard the M/V Machaca. Photo by Nuno Sa.

288409.name: MacAttack
288409.description: Mac Attack was tagged by researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution aboard the MV Machaca. He was named by Alec and Lee Sargent in honor of their grandson, Daniel McColl “Mac” Sargent. Alec is a Corporation member of the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution. For more information visit www.camrinbraun.com.

288410.name: Pico
288410.description: Pico was tagged by scientists with the Harte Research Institute’s Center for Sportfish Science and Conservation at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi. “Pico” is named by Patrick Carson.

288412.name: Norris
288412.description: Inspired by her sponsor, Ken Norris was one of the four founders of SeaWorld in 1964. The data we gather on Norris will continue to help us better understand how to protect her and her habitat. It’s all part of SeaWorld’s mission to inspire people to care for marine animals and the oceans they call home.

288413.name: Ema
288413.description: Ema was tagged by a collaboration of researchers from Saving Our Sharks, Texas State Aquarium, INAPESCA and Mote Marine Laboratory. Scientists hope to learn more about the movement patterns, connectivity between populations, feeding behavior and potential breeding areas with regards to the species in this area.

288414.name: Gotham
288414.description: Gotham is named for the fictional city in Batman that is based on New York City. Gotham is a long time nickname for the city.

288415.name: Sam Houston
288415.description: Sam Houston was tagged by scientists at the Harte Research Institute’s Center for Sportfish Science and Conservation at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi. Sam Houston was named after Statesman Samuel Houston. Houston was a governor, lawyer, and military leader and a key figure in the creation of the state of Texas.

288416.name: Bigelow
288416.description: Bigelow was tagged by researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI) aboard the MV Machaca. He was named in honor of the first director of WHOI, Henry Bryant Bigelow, who described 110 new species to science and published over 100 scientific papers. For more information visit www.camrinbraun.com.

288417.name: Gina
288417.description: Gina was tagged by Mote Marine Laboratory scientists. Tracking sharks like Gina at this time of year can teach us about reproduction in this species by possibly providing insight into pupping and/or mating habitat in and around Charlotte Harbor, as well as track her long-term movements outside the area.

288418.name: Margarita
288418.description: Margarita was a solitary nesting female at Ostional, and the first turtle we found that had no eggs or follicles left in her ovaries. We attached the satellite transmitter under the watchful eyes of a TV crew and then sent her on her way. If you are interested in reading about what else we are doing, you can follow our field work on http://plotkinlabtamu.wix.com/plotkinlab#!blog/b7vfl.

288419.name: Holly
288419.description: Holly is the sixth green sea turtle tagged of the 2019 season. Researchers from the Sanibel-Captiva Conservation Foundation tagged Holly after she successfully laid a nest on Sanibel Island, Florida. She will be part of a study to learn more about the post-nesting movements and migratory pathways of green sea turtles that nest on the gulf coast of Florida. All research authorized by Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission.

288420.name: Cyndi
288420.description: Dave Gallo named Cyndi after his wife.

288421.name: Neda
288421.description: Neda is the first turtle tracked by ARCHELON in Kyparissia Bay in 2018. In Greek mythology, Neda was a nymph of waters (nymphs were regarded as divine spirits animating nature). Neda is also the name of a river at the core nesting area of Kyparissia Bay!

288422.name: Iris
288422.description: Iris was rescued by SeaWorld San Diego on June 13, 2012, where she was found dehydrated, malnourished and five pounds underweight. She was subsequently hydrated, hand fed, and provided nutritional supplements. After three months of healing and a great deal of care at SeaWorld's Animal Health and Rescue Center, Iris was returned to her ocean home.

288423.name: Paumanok
288423.description: "Paumanok" is the Native American name for Long Island. Its name means the "island or land that pays tribute." Its name has been mentioned by Walt Whitman in Leaves of Grass and its history has been described in detail by ornithologist/environmentalist Robert C. Murphy in his book "Fish-Shape Paumanok - Nature and Man on Long Island." Name by Jonathan Mead of East Northport via a crowdsourced naming contest with Ellen Yan of Newsday.

288424.name: Gurney
288424.description: Gurney was tagged just off the coast of the historic Gurney Beach Resort. We look forward to tracking this beautiful immature white shark as it grows to maturity.

288427.name: Lexi
288427.description: This female tiger shark was named in honor of Lexi Speight. She was a young shark lover who died at the age of 8 from liver cancer.

288428.name: Mary Lee
288428.description: Mary Lee was named after OCEARCH expedition leader Chris Fischer's mother. “My parents have done so much. I was waiting and waiting for a special shark to name after her and this is truly the most historic and legendary fish I have ever been a part of and it set the tone for Cape Cod,“ says Chris.

288429.name: Dr Pam
288429.description: Dr. Pam was rescued by the California Wildlife Center (CWC) on May 3, 2018, at Escondido Beach in Malibu, CA. She was thin and dehydrated. Dr. Pam was given oral electrolytes as well as received subcutaneous fluids at CWC to stabilize her condition. Supportive care was indicated including nutrition, vitamin supplementation, and hydration.

288430.name: Sylvia
288430.description: Named after Sylvia Earle, American oceanographer, explorer, author, and lecturer.

288431.name: Amagansett
288431.description: In appreciation for all the people of Amagansett who have helped us out throughout Expedition NY 2017, we've named this shark "Amagansett," so now they have their very own shark to follow!

288432.name: Gisela
288432.description: Gisela was named for Gisela Haschke Lyons wife, mother and grandmother who never met an animal she did not immediately love.

288434.name: Lampiao
288434.description: Lampião's was named after the most famous bandit leader of the Cangaço. Cangaço was a form of banditry endemic to the Brazilian Northeast in the 1920s and 1930s. Lampião's exploits turned him into a 'folk hero', the Brazilian equivalent of Jesse James. A fan, Ellen Pereira, of Cat Dealer Sotreq in Brazil named the tiger shark

288435.name: Gnaraloo
288435.description: Gnaraloo is a famous coastline and surf break in Western Australia.

288436.name: Thetis
288436.description: The seventh turtle tracked this summer. Thetis is a sea goddess in Greek mythology (Nereides), daughter of Nereus and grand-daughter of Tethys. She gave birth to Achilles, the well-known hero of the Trojan war.

288437.name: Vader
288437.description: Vader was tagged by researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution aboard the MV Machaca. He was named by Phoebe Thorrold, a 9 year old ocean enthusiast from Falmouth, MA. For more information visit www.camrinbraun.com.

288438.name: Peggy
288438.description: This female tiger shark is named in honor of Peggy Sloan from the North Carolina Aquariums who hosted OCEARCH during the 2016 North Carolina Expedition and was our greater supporter in the region.

288439.name: Chris Nic
288439.description: Chris Nic was tagged during the 2nd Annual Shark’s Eye Tournament and Festival, which is an all catch and release shark tournament held in Montauk, NY. This shark was captured by Joe Gaviola and the crew of the Free Nicky and named after Joe’s two daughters Christine and Nicole.

288440.name: Melodi
288440.description: Melodi was found nesting at Rio Oro beach after a heavy thunderstorm. She laid a clutch of 92 eggs and the ultrasound images showed us that she had no structures left in either her ovaries or oviducts, which means she should soon start her post-nesting migration.

288441.name: Bill Nye
288441.description: Bill Nye the Science Shark was tagged by Eric Ozolins in collaboration with scientists at the Harte Research Institute’s Center for Sportfish Science and Conservation at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi. Bill Nye the Science Shark was named for Billy Nye the Science Guy, an American science educator, comedian, television presenter, and scientist, given his interest in shark research at TAMU-CC.

288443.name: Gareth
288443.description: Gareth was tagged by researcher at BioPixel Oceans Foundation.

288444.name: Buddy
288444.description: Buddy, named by fans of Caterpillar dealer Holt after Buddy Holly, a singer/songwriter from Texas. Buddy is the first shark tagged during Expedition Gulf of Mexico.

288445.name: Encantada
288445.description: David Acuña from the Charles Darwin Foundation named her Encantada. Encantada is the nickname of the Galapagos National Park.

288446.name: Captain Wayne
288446.description: Captain Wayne was tagged by scientists with the Harte Research Institute’s Center for Sportfish Science and Conservation at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi, during a research cruise on the Scat Cat of the Fisherman’s Wharf. “Captain Wayne” the mako was named by the Johnson family after Wayne Timmerman, an avid outdoorsman whose favorite place to be is on the water.

288447.name: Nemo
288447.description: Captain Brett McBride named Nemo because of the deformity on her pectoral fin.

288449.name: Orlandinho
288449.description: This shark was tagged by André Afonso of Departamento de Pesca e Aquicultura & Universidade Federal Rural de Pernambuco and Yuri Niella as part of a collaboration to tag tiger sharks that started in 2014.

288450.name: Big Kahuna
288450.description: Big Kahuna was tagged during the 2nd Annual Shark’s Eye Tournament and Festival, which is an all catch and release shark tournament held in Montauk, NY. This shark was captured by Joe Gaviola and the crew of the Free Nicky and named by the school children at the Montauk School.

288451.name: Johnny
288451.description: Johnny is a mature male blue shark caught and tagged by researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution aboard the M/V Machaca. He was named by Max Kaplan after a close friend who also loved ocean exploration. Photo by Nuno Sa.

288452.name: Michelle
288452.description: Cat Products named Michelle, with the help of OCEARCH fan Kay Brimage-Minkel, after Michele Bachelet, the first female President of Chile.

288454.name: Amy
288454.description: Amy is named after Amy Kuehner. Carl and Amy Kuehner have done so much for the world it's impossible to describe in less than a novel. From Carl's Chairmanship of the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation (NFWF), to their support of OCEARCH through some of our most difficult times, the Kuehners have "walked the walk" in giving back to our planet. They have given time, treasure, and unbridled positive energy while selflessly supporting the future of our land, ocean and all the creatures that inhabit earth. It's a privilege to be able to name a shark after Amy as a sign of gratitude for all they both have done.

288455.name: SouthJaw
288455.description: SouthJaw is a juvenile male Tiger Shark tagged by scientists at the University of South Alabama (USA) and the Dauphin Island Sea Lab. SouthJaw was named by USA undergraduate students as a tribute to SouthPaw, the University Mascot.

288456.name: Kekoa
288456.description: Kekoa means brave. Kekoa was tagged by the Maui Ocean center, which is the Hawaiian Aquarium, dedicated to promoting fostering and understanding of the Hawaiian Marine environment and the relationship to the host culture to that environment. They are advocates for better understanding of sharks, rays and Hawaiian green Sea Turtles.

288459.name: Clara
288459.description: Named in honor of Clara Barton, founder of the American Red Cross. In 1893, a powerful hurricane struck the Lowcountry coast, killing 2,000 residents. Clara led the “Sea Islands Relief Effort” helping Lowcountry residents survive and rebuild from the devastating hurricane.

288460.name: Redemption
288460.description: Chris Fischer named Redemption after their expedition was briefly shut down by the South African government due to a shark attack.

288461.name: Harmony
288461.description: Sad pictures of the destruction in Houston and the Caribbean islands by the two recent hurricanes have haunted us, and we named our 8th turtle “Harmony”, inspired by a Houstonian student affected by Hurricane Harvey. In her own words: “Houston needs all the Harmony we can get with everyone helping each other recover from this devastation.” If you are interested to read about what else we are doing, you can follow our field work on http://plotkinlabtamu.wix.com/plotkinlab#!blog/b7vfl.

288462.name: Duke
288462.description: Duke was tagged by researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI) aboard the MV Machaca. He was named by Elizabeth Leatherman, a friend, and supporter of WHOI, in honor of legendary Hawaiian waterman Duke Kahanamoku. For more information on the science being conducted with this tagging effort, visit www.camrinbraun.com.

288463.name: Sally
288463.description: Sally is a mature, reproductive female American alligator living in the Okefenokee Swamp, the largest blackwater swamp in North America. Sally successfully nested in 2017 and currently has another incubating nest from the 2018 season. She has been closely monitored using Moultrie Game Cameras since January of 2018 and researchers continue to observe her behavior. Sally appears to be an Alpha female in her area of the Okefenokee Swamp and is particularly sassy, making her an excellent mother as she guards her young!

288465.name: Yinzer
288465.description: Yinzer was tagged by researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI) aboard the MV Machaca. He was named by the Mandella family who is both avid shark followers and fluent in Pittsburghese. For more information on the science being conducted with this tagging effort, visit www.camrinbraun.com.

288466.name: Mahkato
288466.description: Mahkato was tagged by researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution aboard the MV Machaca. He was named by Megan DuVal, a 13-year-old future marine biologist and shark lover from Salt Lake City, Utah. The name Mahkato comes from the language of the Dakota tribe. In this language, it means “blue-green earth”, which refers to the blue-green color of the clay in that region. For more information visit www.camrinbraun.com.

288467.name: Cisco
288467.description: Cisco was named for Cisco Beach on Nantucket and for our partner Cisco Brewery who created the Shark Tracker Light Lager to support our research.

288468.name: Gale
288468.description: Gale is a female short-finned pilot whale that was brought to SeaWorld Orlando as part of a mass stranding of other cetaceans off the coast of St. Petersburg, Fla. in July 2017. After a short rehabilitation, she was successfully returned off the west coast of Florida in August 2017.

288469.name: Bruin
288469.description: Bruin is a young of the year white shark tagged on August 12, 2017 during Expedition New York. This shark was named for the students at the Brunswick school in Greenwitch, CT so they can have a shark to track. Go Bruin's! #DontFearTheFin

288470.name: Sawtooth
288470.description: Sawtooth was tagged by researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution aboard the MV Machaca. He was named after the Sawtooth Mountains of central Idaho by Mrs. Etcheverry’s 8th grade science class at Bear Lake Middle School (Idaho, USA). For more information visit www.camrinbraun.com.

288471.name: Georgia
288471.description: Georgia was the first shark tagged during Expedition Jacksonville 2016. OCEARCH has ongoing collaborations with Bryan Frazer from the South Carolina Department of Natural Resources, and this shark will add to his sample size. Georgia was named in honor of the state she was tagged in, by suggestions during the Periscope live streaming.

288472.name: Floreana
288472.description: David Acuna of the Charles Darwin Foundation named Floreana after the island in Galapagos.

288473.name: Yolanda
288473.description: Yolanda was named by Cat Products after Yolanda Kakabadse Navarro, the former president of the World Wildlife Fund International and International Union for Conservation of Nature. She dedicated her life and career to the protection and awareness of environmental issues, not only in Ecuador but worldwide.

288474.name: Philip
288474.description: Philip was named by Olie after his father.

288475.name: Oscar
288475.description: Oscar is a mature male mako shark caught and tagged by researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution aboard the M/V Machaca. Note: Photo is not of Oscar. Photo is previously tagged mako shark Daymond.

288476.name: Nova
288476.description: Nova is the first white shark OCEARCH has ever tagged in Canadian waters. He was tagged during our Nova Scotia expedition not far from the town of Lunenburg. He is named in honor of all the wonderful people of Nova Scotia who have been so welcoming and supportive of OCEARCH’s work.

288477.name: Posidonia
288477.description: Posidonia takes her name from the endemic to the Mediterranean sea seagrass species, Posidonia oceanica. The Posidonia ecosystem provides home to many species of fish, as well as shelter to the eggs of many organisms. For sea turtles, it provides habitat and feeding ground. The genus Posidonia is named after Poseidon, the Greek god of the seas!

288478.name: Susan
288478.description: Susan laid her eggs right in front of a huge beach resort and was a little bit disoriented by the hotel’s light when she crawled back to the water. She laid a total of 114 eggs and we are looking forward to seeing her travel to her next destination. If you are interested to read about what else we are doing, you can follow our field work on http://plotkinlabtamu.wix.com/plotkinlab#!blog/b7vfl.

288479.name: Vera
288479.description: The sixth turtle tracked this summer. Vera's name derives from verus, meaning verity and faith.

288480.name: Hampton
288480.description: Hampton is named in honor of the Hampton’s community and collaborating science partner, South Hampton Schools.

288481.name: Edith
288481.description: Edith is our very last turtle for this season and named in honor of the person who showed the most spirit across our school outreach program to increase #OceanLiteracy. If you are interested to read about what else we are doing, you can follow our field work on http://plotkinlabtamu.wix.com/plotkinlab#!blog/b7vfl.

288482.name: Luna
288482.description: At 15-feet long, Luna is the second biggest white shark we’ve tagged in the North Atlantic. She’s named for the incredible people of Lunenburg, Nova Scotia.

288483.name: Kate
288483.description: Kate is the third green sea turtle tagged of the 2019 season. Through a collaborative effort, researchers from the Conservancy of Southwest Florida and the Sanibel-Captiva Conservation Foundation tagged Kate after she successfully laid a nest on Sanibel Island, Florida.  She had been previously encountered laying eggs two years earlier in 2017 on the same beach. Kate will be part of a study to learn more about the post-nesting movements and migratory pathways of green sea turtles that nest on the gulf coast of Florida. All research authorized by Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission.

288484.name: Carolina
288484.description: This female tiger shark is named after North Carolina, the state in which she was tagged.

288485.name: Madeline
288485.description: Madeline was tagged by scientists at the Harte Research Institute’s Center for Sportfish Science and Conservation at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi. Madeline meaning “little girl” is named after Madeline Stunz - a five-year-old future veterinarian wanting to specialize in the care of sharks.

288486.name: Nicole
288486.description: Named after Mate Alex Snow sister-in-law.

288489.name: Lesley
288489.description: Todd Goggins named Lesley after his Grandmother.

288490.name: Wyatt
288490.description: Wyatt was tagged by scientists at the Harte Research Institute’s Center for Sportfish Science and Conservation at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi. Wyatt meaning “brave and strong” is named after Wyatt Montgomery of Houston, TX. Wyatt (the human) is a young shark enthusiast that has been intrigued with sharks from a very young age.

288491.name: Miss Michalove
288491.description: "Miss Michalove" was the first tiger shark tagged by the cooperative project. Captain Chip Michalove named her in honor of his mother who passed from cancer in 1998. She pushed Captain Chip to follow his true passion and inspired him to stick with what he loves.

288492.name: Freo
288492.description: Named after Fremantle, a major Australian port city in Western Australia located at the mouth of the Swan River.

288493.name: Fritz
288493.description: “Fritz” was named in honor of former US Senator Ernest “Fritz” Hollings who was a champion for the conservation of natural resources in SC as well as protection of ocean resources. He pushed to establish the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) and was involved in the passage of the National Coastal Zone Management Act, the Marine Mammal Protection Act, the Ocean Dumping Act and the Fishery Conservation and Management Act.

288494.name: Katya (tiger shark)
288494.description: Dr. Adam Barnett of TropWATER at James Cook University in partnership with OCEARCH tagged Katya on Batt Reef, Queensland, Australia

288495.name: Anne Morrow
288495.description: "Anne Morrow" was named in honor of biologist Bryan Frazier's wife, Anne, who recently gave birth to their second child.

288496.name: Nico
288496.description: Captain Brett McBride named Nico after his son.

288497.name: Reveille
288497.description: This Scalloped hammerhead is named after Reveille the official mascot of Texas A&M University. Reveille is the most revered dog on the campus. If she is in class and barks while the professor is teaching, the class is to be immediately dismissed. This was the 4rd shark tagged during Expedition Gulf of Mexico.

288498.name: Courage
288498.description: Chris Fischer named Courage at the end of the expedition in South Africa.

288499.name: Montauk
288499.description: Montauk is the first white shark tagged during Expedition NY 2016. She is the young of the year and will add to data that will determine the birthing site for the Atlantic White Shark.

288500.name: Einstein
288500.description: Einstein was tagged by scientists at the Harte Research Institute’s Center for Sportfish Science and Conservation at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi. Einstein was named by Debbie and Sam Isaacs, in honor of the famous scientist Albert Einstein. Einstein was tagged near an oil and gas platform off the Texas coast.

288501.name: Diane
288501.description: Diane was named after Diane Lantz-Rickard, Caterpillar Global Brand Marketing Manager, who is passionate about the ocean and understands that a healthy ocean depends on healthy shark populations.

288502.name: Red
288502.description: Red was rescued by Marin Animal Rescue on Feb. 27, 2018, from Redondo Beach, CA.  He was taken to the Marine Mammal Care Center Los Angeles for treatment. Red was hypothermic and lethargic. Electrolytes were administered to help stabilize his condition. Red was returned to the ocean on May 16, 2018, approximately eight miles off the coast of San Diego. Red was rehabilitated in collaboration with the MMHSRP under NMFS permit #18786.

288503.name: Warne
288503.description: Warne was tagged by researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI) aboard the MV Machaca. He was named in honor of the Warne Family Foundation, a generous sponsor of shark research at WHOI. For more information visit www.camrinbraun.com.

288504.name: Cypress
288504.description: Cypress is an adult, reproductive female American alligator living in the Okefenokee Swamp, the largest blackwater swamp in North America. By collecting data on her movements using satellite tags we are hoping to better understand how female alligators use the swamp ecosystem and how their home ranges vary with seasonality. We are also hoping to use her movement data to locate her nesting site.

288505.name: Ningaloo
288505.description: Ningaloo was named after the Ningaloo Reef in West Australia where she was tagged.

288506.name: Perth
288506.description: Perth the tiger shark is named after the largest city in West Australia, Perth.

288507.name: Audrey Laine
288507.description: Audrey Laine is an adult, reproductive female American alligator living in the Okefenokee Swamp, the largest blackwater swamp in North America. She was named Audrey Laine after one of her sponsors, Audrey Laine Seymour, a Blackshear native. By collecting data on Audrey's movements using satellite tags, we are hoping to better understand how female alligators use the swamp ecosystem and how their home ranges vary with seasonality. We are also hoping to use her movement data to locate her nest!

288508.name: Faith
288508.description: We had moved to a different nesting beach (Hacienda Baru) and after three nights with many poachers on the beach, we were able to outrun them and found Faith. She did not have any follicles or eggs left in her ovaries and oviducts, so she is seemingly done nesting for the season. If you are interested to read about what else we are doing, you can follow our field work on http://plotkinlabtamu.wix.com/plotkinlab#!blog/b7vfl.

288509.name: YETI
288509.description: YETI is a female white shark named for our longtime partner, YETI Coolers, who has supported our expeditions for years. With 4 pings in less than 24 hours, we expect this shark to be a “pinger.” We can’t wait to see where she goes!

288510.name: Zac
288510.description: Sam Young named the tiger shark Zac in love memory of his brother Zachariah Young, who died after being attacked by a tiger shark in Reicks Point, NSW.

288511.name: Buzz
288511.description: Buzz was tagged by researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution aboard the MV Machaca. He was named by WHOI Trustee David Scully. For more information visit www.camrinbraun.com.

288512.name: Albert
288512.description: Brett McBride, OCEARCH Captain and Fishing Master, named Albert after his father.

288513.name: Guayasamin
288513.description: Named after Escuela Oswaldo Guayasamin, the local school Chris Fischer, Alex Hearn (TIRN), David Acuna (FCD), and Yasmania (PNG) visited during Expedition Galapagos.

288515.name: The Judge
288515.description: The Judge was tagged by scientists of The Nature Conservancy using a SPOT tag during a shark fisheries-independent monitoring cruise off Sarasota Bay in Florida in collaboration with Mote Marine Laboratory. “The Judge” is named after Judge Roy Bean, a legendary Justice of Peace who called himself "The Law West of the Pecos [River]" in the late 1800s along the Rio Grande on southwest Texas.

288516.name: Daymond
288516.description: Daymond was tagged by recreational anglers Eric Ozolins and Ricky Torres working with the scientists at the Harte Research Institute’s Center for Sportfish Science and Conservation at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi. “Daymond” is named after Daymond John, an American entrepreneur and investor on ABC’s Shark Tank, given his interest in shark research at TAMU-CC.

288518.name: Duval
288518.description: This male tiger shark was named after Duval Country where the team has been working off shore during Expedition Jacksonville 2016. This was the 4th tiger shark tagged during #ExpeditionJax.

288519.name: Rocky Mazzanti
288519.description: Rocky Mazzanti was named by the Team at eMazzanti Technologies in honor of their ocean-loving Shih Tzu, who recently passed away. She was tagged by Tom Burns and Eric Savetsky aboard the MV Endurance. This tagged whale shark is part of the TOTEM Project based at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution. For more information visit the TOTEM Project website (https://simonthorrold.com/totem/).

288520.name: Bindi
288520.description: Named by Caterpillar after Bindi Irwin, wildlife conservationist who inherited her father’s passion for wildlife and conservation.

288521.name: Manuelita
288521.description: On this trip, we established connectivity between Cocos and Galapagos, when we detected a silky shark at Darwin that we tagged at Cocos on the 2011 expedition. Although Cocos and Galapagos are marine protected areas, once the sharks begin their migration from one site to the other, they are vulnerable to fishing gear. We are naming this silky shark Manuelita to highlight the connectivity between Galapagos and Cocos and to begin building a case for a protected “shark swim way” between the two reserves.

288689.name: Sydney
288689.description: Sydney is the first white shark tagged by OCEARCH during Expedition Nova Scotia in the fall of 2019. He's the first white shark to get a comprehensive health assessment and SPOT tag in the Cape Breton region of Nova Scotia.

289874.name: Murdoch
289874.description: Murdoch is the second white shark tagged by OCEARCH during Expedition Nova Scotia in 2019. He was named by Southern Tide who gave naming rights away to their social community. The name Murdoch has Gaelic roots meaning "of the sea." He was tagged off Cape Breton, Nova Scotia where there is a log of Gaelic heritage.

290985.name: Unama'ki
290985.description: Unama'ki is what the indigenous Mi'kmaq people of Nova Scotia call Cape Breton and it means "land of the fog." As a big mature female, Unama'ki has the potential to lead us to the site where she gives birth and exposes a new white shark nursery.

303706.name: Doug
303706.description: Dough was tagged as part of a collaboration between scientists at: Saving Our Sharks, Texas State Aquarium, INAPESCA, Mote Marine. Scientists will be looking for movement patterns, conenctivity, feeding & breeding areas.

303707.name: Mario
303707.description: Mario was tagged by collaborating scientists at Saving Our Sharks, Texas State Aquarium, INAPESCA andMote Marine. Researchers will be looking for movement patterns, connectivity, feeding & breeding areas.

303708.name: Caper
303708.description: Caper was tagged by OCEARCH during Expedition Nova Scotia in 2019. She is named for the people of Cape Breton who call themselves Capers.

305537.name: Max
305537.description: This fish was tagged by Dr. Camrin Braun and Dr. Peter Gaube from the University of Washington as part of the Ocean Twilight Zone project (https://twilightzone.whoi.edu/) at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution and Operation Deep Drop, in partnership with Wildlife Computers (https://wildlifecomputers.com/). Max was named by Dr. Peter Gaube's oldest son who is an avid fish fanatic with an insatiable interest in the oceans. For more information and to contribute to Operation Deep Drop visit the GoFundMe page.

305547.name: Shaw
305547.description: White shark shaw is named after Mike Shaw, the curator of fishes at SeaWorld San Diego for over 40 years and the initiator of white shark research at SeaWorld. He was tagged as part of OCEARCH's 2019 expedition to Nova Scotia.

305548.name: Ferg
305548.description: Ferg is an adult white shark named in memory of Ray "Ferg" Ferguson, one of the founders of OCEARCH's incredible partner Costa Sunglasses. His legacy lives on through the support Costa continues to give to our mission to ensure future generations have healthy oceans.

305549.name: Scotia
305549.description: Whtie shark Scotia was tagged as part of Expedition Nova Scotia in 2019. She is named for all of the wonderful people of Nova Scotia who have been so supportive of the work OCEARCH is doing off their coast.

305550.name: Teazer
305550.description: White shark Teazer is named after a ghost ship, called the Young Teazer, that lore has it returns to the Mahone Bay area every year. Just like the ship returns, OCEARCH will be watching closely to see if white shark Teazer also returns on a regular basis.

308724.name: Ironbound
308724.description: Ironbound is named after West Ironbound Island near Lunenburg, Nova Scotia. He is the 53rd white shark SPOT-tagged by OCEARCH in the Northwest Atlantic Ocean.

308731.name: Vimy
308731.description: Vimy is named after the Battle of Vimy Ridge, where Canadian forces fought with tenacity to prove themselves as a rising nation to the rest of the world. He is the 11th and final shark tagged during OCEARCH 2019 expedition to Nova Scotia.

309147.name: Oliver
309147.description: This fish was tagged by Dr. Camrin Braun and Dr. Peter Gaube from the University of Washington as part of the Ocean Twilight Zone project at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution and Operation Deep Drop, in partnership with Wildlife Computers. Oliver was named by Dr. Simon Thorrold (WHOI) after his grandfather who was an avid fisherman and passionate about ocean conservation. For more information and to contribute to Operation Deep Drop visit the GoFundMe page.

309149.name: Simone
309149.description: This fish was tagged by Dr. Camrin Braun and Dr. Peter Gaube from the University of Washington as part of the Ocean Twilight Zone project at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution and Operation Deep Drop, in partnership with Wildlife Computers. Simone was named after the late wife of famous French explorer and scientist, Jacques Cousteau. Simone Melchior Cousteau was the first female scuba diver and aquanaut and played a key role in the operation at sea. For more information and to contribute to Operation Deep Drop visit the GoFundMe page.

309150.name: Anthony
309150.description: This fish was tagged by Dr. Camrin Braun and Dr. Peter Gaube from the University of Washington as part of the Ocean Twilight Zone project at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution and Operation Deep Drop, in partnership with Wildlife Computers. Anthony was named after Capt. Anthony "Tony" DiGiulian, an accomplished angler and guide who has dedicated his life to helping people experience the joy of fishing through his work with numerous foundations and organizations. For more information and to contribute to Operation Deep Drop visit the GoFundMe page.

367202.name: Bluenose
367202.description: White shark Bluenose was tagged at West Ironbound Island near Lunenburg, Nova Scotia. He is named after the famous schooner that used to dominate the Canadian waters as both a fishing and racing vessel. The ship has become a part of Nova Scotia's identity.

405769.name: Grizz
